--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.deselect_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Remove edges from selection. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.deselect_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Remove edges from selection. title: >- [Graph.deselect_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Remove edges from selection. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Remove edges from selection. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24283-L24354){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.deselect_edges(edge_ids) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Deselect edges](../assets/graphs/deselect-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A grid whose edges are labeled with their ids 1 to 7. Before: edges 1, 2, and 4 (A–B, B–C, B–E) are selected in the accent color. After deselect_edges with id 2, edge B–C returns to plain and edges 1 and 4 stay selected." width="100%"} Removes the given edges from the current edge selection, leaving the rest of the selection intact. The edges themselves are not touched; only their selected state changes. Edges in the list that are not currently selected are ignored. This is a quick way to carve exceptions out of a selection -- for example, selecting all edges around a node with `select_edges_by_node()` and then deselecting one that should survive a following `delete_edges_ws()`. To drop the whole selection, use `clear_selection()` instead. A node selection is left as it is. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer edge IDs to remove from the selection. IDs that are not selected, or that match no edge at all, are silently ignored (no error is raised). An empty list leaves the selection unchanged. Edge IDs can be found with `get_edge_ids()`, `get_selected_edge_ids()`, or the `id` column of `get_edge_df()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting every edge in a 5-edge cycle and then deselecting one leaves the other four selected: ::: {#c80ea631 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) all_edges = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.select_edges_by_id(all_edges) graph.deselect_edges([all_edges[0]]) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: Deselection is useful for protecting an edge from a bulk operation. Here every edge touching "B" is selected, the `B-C` edge is deselected, and the rest are deleted -- so `B-C` and the unrelated `C-D` remain: ::: {#27c5f31a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) .select_edges_by_node(["B"]) ) b_c = graph.get_edge_ids()[1] # IDs follow creation order: A-B, B-C, C-D graph.deselect_edges([b_c]).delete_edges_ws() graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
